recipes.name: Simple Pouch Potatoes
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 pinch garlic powder, or to taste
1 pinch dried oregano, or to taste
0.5 cup light butter-flavored spread (such as I Can't Believe It's Not Butter ® Light)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease 4 aluminum foil sheets with cooking spray.
Divide potatoes evenly among the prepared aluminum foil sheets; season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and oregano. Place 2 tablespoons butter-flavored spread over each set of potatoes.
Create packets by folding and sealing the aluminum foil. Place the 4 foil packets on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes are tender and easily pierced with a fork, 55 minutes to 1 hour. Drain melted butter-flavored spread before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Pouch Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Yummy butter flavor is baked into chunks of tender red potatoes seasoned with garlic powder and oregano in this no-fuss side dish.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is so easy and good. My family loves it. I also add cheese, diced onion and even have put a small piece of bacon on the top. I also spray the foil with pam....

Very simple; I do recommend one revierer's suggestion to microwave the potatoes for 3 minutes prior to grilling; this will allow them to be cooked in the time it takes to grill your chicken, or whatever meat of preference. I did not use any butter at all and didn't miss it. Just used the potatoes, some chopped red onion, bacon bits, kosher salt, pepper.

Great recipe that's low in fat! I did mine on the grill. I sprayed the bottom of a foil packet with Pam to prevent the potatoes from sticking. I left out the oregano (personal preference) and added some vidalia onion. I used minced garlic vs. garlic powder. There's nothing simpler and these go great with BBQ chicken.

A favorite in my family! I do these a little different, I slice the potatoes into large slices, place a thin slice of onion in between each slice with a thin pat of butter, then I salt & pepper the entire thing. Try a splash of Frank's Red Hot over the top - they're DELICIOUS!! :)
we've been doing this on the grill for years--a couple of minutes in the microwave with the potatoes before you put them in the pouch saves a lot of time on the grill or in the oven.
I have been making these for years...good for camping too. You can just throw them into the coals but dont forget to turn over. Sometimes I add smoke sausage and onions to the mix.
Used quartered petite yellow potatoes in one pouch w/butter and recommended seasonings. Baked as directed, and they came out creamy and delicious!
I loved this recipe- got me a good start. Rather than the low fat version, I drizzled EVOO, and a couple tbsp of butter were thrown in the pack. I added fresh basil, oregano, and garlic as well.

I have been making this for over 30 years, when camping, either on a grill or in the coals of an open fire. I add diced onion, cheese and often a egg, lightly stirred to each packet. My family love this quick easy recipe.

I have made this for years - on the grill! It's such an easy way to make potatoes while the meat is grilling. Add sliced onions! Cook the packet until the potatoes are fork-tender, flipping them over once in awhile (if the foil packet is super-tight) to be sure they are getting evenly done. I wouldn't use oregano, but only because I don't care for oregano. Garlic/salt/pepper/butter is plenty.

Not only does the recipe sound good the reviews and tweaking make my mouth water. can't wait to make it. Thanks for sharing!
My family loves this recipe! We make it when whenever we go camping. I also add red and green peppers and sliced garlic.
